correctness.rationale: Euclidean polarity transforms projection inradius into inverse central cube-section circumradius. For all ordered normal components \(a\ge b\ge c\ge0\), an exhaustive vertex argument yields \(R^2=2+((b+c)/a)^2\) when a>=b+c and \(R^2=2+((a-c)/b)^2\) otherwise. Spherical event cones have the rays and determinants \(s^2\) stated in RESULT.md; 48 chambers and the classical triple-vector solid-angle formula produce exactly the two arctan denominators and endpoints. Directly verified 1,329 rational plane sections and 500 distinct geometric planar hull projections, plus 80,000 Haar samples. The infinite claim rests on explicit proof; degeneracies covered by continuity/nullity.

originality.rationale: Inspected the initiating 2026 width-law manuscript in its available entirety, the historical primary 1997 regular-polytope projection manuscript, relevant accessible random-section abstracts, and current indexed mathematical records. Compared polar dual, breadth and exact parameters: none of the accessed results states or demonstrably implies the exact distribution of the projected octahedron inradius. An important 2026 manuscript on random section diameters remains full-text inaccessible and an unindexed equivalent result is possible; these unresolved risks are expressly retained, rather than declared absent.

No independent external expert validation of novelty has been performed.

value.rationale: The inradius is an invariant of every planar convex projection, and its full Haar distribution for the elementary regular octahedron is a motivated canonical benchmark complementing the established width and face-count laws. The result gives a complete normalized all-threshold exact elementary law with two nontrivial cone regimes, not a routine single-angle computation or selected numerical parameter. It yields quantiles and reproducible calibration data for random cube sections without claiming any higher-dimensional or universal theorem.
